I grepped the V7 tree for `weightedSum_apply`-style lemmas and found none. I also counted how often `weightedSum` is unfolded by hand in simp calls (28 occurrences in 9 files). The one finding is the missing coordinate-evaluation simp lemma for `weightedSum`. I did not run Lean, so I am not claiming the proposed lemma has compiled. It would be a `rfl` proof. findings.declaration: V7.Stage4AboveTwoIdentity.alpha_weighted_primal (also alpha_weighted_dual and the zero case of dualP_map)
findings.problem: `weightedSum` is a plain `def` that returns `fun j => ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, a i * X i j`. There is no simp lemma that evaluates it at a coordinate, and I found no `weightedSum_apply`, `weightedSum_succ` or `weightedSum_zero` anywhere in ParameterFreeGradient. So each proof here (lines 63-64, 81-82, 114-115) has to `ext j` and then unfold the whole definition by name with `simp only [weightedSum, ...]`. The same unfolding appears in about 28 simp calls across 9 V7 files (ResidualAlgebra, Stage3BelowTwo/Dual, Stage3BelowTwo/Identity, Stage4AboveTwoDualPhase/DualEnergy and others). Unfolding exposes the raw `Finset.sum` form instead of a stable normal form, and each caller then has to finish with `Finset.sum_eq_single` or `Finset.sum_range_one` by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Next to the definition of `weightedSum` (or in ResidualAlgebra) add a coordinate-evaluation simp lemma: `@[simp] lemma weightedSum_apply (n a X j) : weightedSum n a X j = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, a i * X i j := rfl`. I would also consider `@[simp] weightedSum_zero` and a `weightedSum_succ` stating `weightedSum (n+1) a X = weightedSum n a X + a n • X n`. The `rfl` proofs and the exact statements are unverified. Then rewrite the three proofs here as `ext j; simp [weightedSum_apply, ...]`. Keep the raw definition out of simp sets.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical, discoverable rewrite for evaluating `weightedSum`. Callers no longer unfold the definition by name, and proofs no longer depend on its internal `fun j => ∑ ...` shape. Many near-identical `simp [weightedSum, ...]` calls in the V7 proofs can then be shortened, and a later change to the definition affects one lemma instead of every caller.

evidence.excerpt:
noncomputable def weightedSum (n : ℕ) (a : ScalarSeq) (X : VectorSeq d) : Point d :=
  fun j => ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, a i * X i j
